article.headline: Sacha Baron Cohen revives Ali G for misguided comedy film Who Iz I
article.summary: Sacha Baron Cohen brings back his iconic 2000s character Ali G in the new film Ali G: Who Iz I?, which attempts to navigate modern culture through a series of elaborate pranks.
article.body:
Ali G discovers a fax from HBO offering him a multimillion-dollar deal to return to television, only to arrive in Los Angeles and realize the offer expired 22 years ago. Left without prospects after squandering his previous earnings and moving into his late grandmother's flat, the character attempts to pivot to a career as a TikTok content creator. He films videos featuring mukbangs and outfit hauls alongside local politicians and retired military personnel in an effort to regain his former fame.

The film marks Sacha Baron Cohen’s directorial debut and features a mix of live-ammo hoaxes rather than a traditional narrative structure. By returning to a character that rose to prominence in the early 2000s, the project forces Baron Cohen to confront his own fame, as he is now often recognized by the public he seeks to prank. To manage this challenge, the production utilizes body doubles and covert reshoots to pull off its high-stakes satirical stunts.

According to TheWrap, the movie struggles to find relevance in a culture that has moved past the character’s original style of humor. TheGuardian notes that the project also incorporates performances from previous characters, including the security consultant Erran Morad and liberal activist Dr. Nira Cain-N’Degrocello. One unnamed Republican leader who appeared in the film has already expressed intentions to sue the comedian, labeling the experience an embarrassment.

Ultimately, the production relies on clarifying who is in on the jokes, appearing to address a new generation of viewers who may be unfamiliar with the original series. The film captures a performer attempting to force his legacy into a fragmented, modern media landscape where his original shock tactics face different societal standards.

article.headline: Riquelme Fillipi snatches 90th-minute equalizer to rescue Inter Miami against Cincinnati
article.summary: Inter Miami and FC Cincinnati fought to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday as Riquelme Fillipi scored in the final minute to share the points.
article.body: Riquelme Fillipi emerged from the bench in the 83rd minute to salvage a point for Inter Miami, firing home a crucial equalizer in the 90th minute. The dramatic finish followed a frantic second-half turnaround that saw all four goals scored in the final 30 minutes of play at Nu Stadium. Following a scoreless first half that saw Lionel Messi receive a yellow card in the 44th minute, Luis Suarez broke the deadlock in the 61st minute off an assist from Casemiro. The opening goal electrified the home crowd, but Miami’s lead proved short-lived as Cincinnati shifted the momentum late in the match. The visitors capitalized on a tiring defense, with Kenji Mboma Dem leveling the score in the 80th minute. Just six minutes later, Samuel Gidi connected on a Tyler Barlow assist to put Cincinnati ahead 2-1, silencing the Florida supporters. Facing a potential defeat, Inter Miami maintained pressure until Fillipi converted a delivery from Rodrigo De Paul in the dying moments of regulation. The draw highlights a test for Miami as they continue their Eastern Conference campaign, while Cincinnati’s late surge underscores their desperate pursuit of a playoff position. Goal.com reports that despite the offensive flurry, disciplinary issues plagued Miami, resulting in three separate yellow cards during the match. With the result finalized at 2-2, both teams leave the pitch having traded leads in a match defined by second-half chaos. While Suarez and Fillipi proved decisive for the hosts, the team now looks to regain defensive stability following a difficult night where they conceded two goals in quick succession.
